counterfactual_missing_items: No melanocytic nevi or leptomeningeal melanosis to support Neurocutaneous Melanosis
No subependymal/periventricular SEGA-typical location or immunophenotype
No rhabdoid morphology or INI1/SMARCB1 loss to support Rhabdoid Tumor
decisive_items: TSC1 gene mutation (15 exon c.1690 G > T, p.E564*)
Subcortical tubers in white matter of frontal lobes
response.rationale: R4 uniquely integrates a pathogenic TSC1 mutation with cardiac rhabdomyoma, subcortical tubers, depigmented spots, and seizures; the other options explain only single lesions or nonspecific histology. R5 has posterior-fossa histology but no syndromic correlation and brachyury/EMA/pan-CK staining is not typical for rhabdoid tumor; R1 is a single lesion, R2 lacks raw support and SEGA criteria, R3 lacks melanosis.

rejected.why: No raw support; depigmented spots are hypopigmented rather than melanocytic and no melanosis/nevi are described.
Cardiac rhabdomyoma is one component of TSC and cannot account for the TSC1 mutation, brain tubers, seizures, or skin findings.
Has no raw support spans; the posterior fossa location and brachyury/EMA/pan-CK-positive high-grade histology do not establish SEGA, and SEGA is only a tumor type, not the overall syndrome.
